Q: Which kind of task to implement to build a thread pool A:

The main reason why you don't want this, is that sleep doesn't consume CPU time. For a thread pool, that is important. Calculating Fibonacci numbers (the unoptimized way) is one way to spend a non-trivial, tunable amount of CPU power. Fib(3) is almost free, Fib(15) is a significant amount of calculation.

Q: How to handle the ... parameter when programming with dplyr A:

The relevant documentation can be found in the ‘rlang’ package under dynamic dots (it’s linked from the other documentation you read).

In a nutshell, you can use rlang::enquos() to capture unevaluated (“defused”) expressions passed as arguments, and you can use the splice operator !!! in place of {{…}} to inject them into supporting functions:

mygroup <- function (data, ...) {
  vars <- rlang::enquos(...)
  data |> group_by(!!!vars)
}

(But in this example you don’t need any of that, you can directly pass ... to dplyr::group_by, just as you did in your my_summarise function.)
